title: Reactive regional switchover and rate-decay protection policy for overload signals
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During regional surges and transient backpressure (429s, connection timeouts, elevated error-rate), we need an automatic, observable mechanism to re-route traffic away from affected capacity while minimizing oscillation and preserving tenant SLAs. Current hard circuit-breaker heuristics are either too eager (false-positive failovers on short spikes) or too slow (degraded tail latency for minutes).

Goal: Implement a reactive switchover controller that: (1) consumes multi-signal inputs (429 rate, timeout count, p95/p99 latency, error-rate); (2) computes a decayed trip score per region+tier+tenant; (3) triggers staged actions (rate-limit, per-tenant probation, regional reroute to alternate tier or model variant) when score crosses thresholds; (4) uses a rate-decay window to avoid flapping and supports manual override and telemetry.

Scope and constraints: Work covers control-plane decision logic, signal ingestion, config API for policies, and small runtime hooks to enforce reroutes and variant selection. This ticket does NOT implement full dashboarding or billing adjustments (separate follow-ups). Must be safe for Dedicated and Hosted modes and respect tenant isolation rules.

Signals and scoring: Proposed input signals and weighting (initial):
- 429 ratio (over 1m, 5m windows) — high weight
- request timeout count (absolute and rate) — high weight
- error-rate 5xx and model-specific decode errors — medium weight
- p95 latency increase relative to baseline — medium weight
- queue depth and token loss alerts from runtime — low weight
Score computed as weighted sum with exponential decay (half-life configurable, default 3m). Add hysteresis: require sustained score > high threshold for activation; sustained score < low threshold for recovery.

Actions and staged fallbacks:
1) Soft throttle: apply tenant-level 429-equivalent admission-limiter when score > soft_thresh for region+tier (minimally invasive).
2) Variant switchover: route new requests to cheaper/ lower-latency model variant (quantized or shorter-context) when score > variant_thresh for N minutes and capacity confirmed on target variant.
3) Regional reroute: when score > hard_thresh, route traffic to alternate region or Dedicated pool according to priority routing table.
4) Probation: upon switchover, place origin region into probation window with decaying score; allow auto-retry after probation if signals subside.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Sensitivity vs false positives: prefer multi-signal fusion and decay to avoid flapping.
- Per-tenant vs global policies: support both; start with global region-tier policy and enable per-tenant overrides only for enterprise tiers to limit blast radius.
- Model-variant compatibility: need mapping of compatible variants and pre-warm requirements to avoid POODLE effects when switching to cold models.
- Observability: must emit events for each action (soft-throttle, variant-switchover, reroute) with context and metrics for downstream incident-runbooks.

Risk mitigation: conservative defaults, staged rollout (canary on low-traffic customers), and kill-switch in control plane. Security review flagged for control-plane policy manipulation — see security_review_required below.
